correctness.rationale: Every noncentral gradient pair is determined by a unique earlier graph neighbor. The six local maximal noncentral two-pair matchings form a hexagon; when the common vertex is paired, the target-square contribution is three isolated vertices and every other square contributes a three-edge collapsible path. All local orders interleave, so the join decomposition and links are exact for every m. Each common-vertex matching vertex has collapsible link for m≥2 and can be deleted by ordinary free-face collapses, leaving the join of m six-cycles. The face polynomial follows by partitioning faces according to whether they contain a common-vertex pair. The standalone package program exhausts actual orders at m=1,2,3; 64 and 768 true free-face pairs are independently checked at m=2,3, with matching face counts and mod-2 homology. No unproved finite-to-infinite extrapolation is used.

value.rationale: This is an infinite-family full integral homotopy and simplicial-collapse classification for a canonical one-vertex bouquet, not a finite checksum. The single-square five-circle wedge becomes one high-dimensional sphere for every m≥2; the structural explanation is collapsibility of the new common-vertex matching links. A full face polynomial and purity result make the exact combinatorial content useful. The obvious disjoint-union theorem yields a different homotopy type and cannot settle the identified-vertex case.
